records.name: People's Music Supply
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit for collectively improvised music. It runs open improvisation labs on Tuesday evenings and a concert series on Wednesdays, and its events page also lists shows by members that the group does not run.
records.what_you_do: Musicians can take part in the open improvisation labs on Tuesday evenings. Listeners can come to the Wednesday concerts. Some events link to a registration page, but the events page does not say whether signing up is needed.

schedule.text: Open improvisation labs run on Tuesday evenings at 7 pm, and the World to Come concert series is on Wednesdays at 5:30 pm.

cost.text: Costs are not listed on the events page.

first_step.how: Email the group to ask about the next Tuesday open improvisation lab at The Living Signal, or join the monthly mailing list from the contact page.
first_step.basis: The contact page invites people to email about open sessions and the labs are listed publicly, but the events page does not say who the labs are for or whether beginners fit.
first_step.what_to_expect: The Tuesday labs take place at The Living Signal at 7 pm, and each one has its own listing on the events page. The page does not say how long a lab runs, who attends, or what it costs, so ask the group before you go.
first_visit_tips: Email the group first to ask whether you need to register.
The next Tuesday lab on the events page is on October 13, 2026.

records.notes: Events page lists 17 items from October to December 2026. Member shows marked non-affiliated are not run by the group and are not used here. The Living Signal street address is not on the site, and one web search did not find it, so no address is recorded. Email decoded from the [at] and [dot] spelling on the contact page; please confirm. Summary and what you do were corrected because the events page shows member shows the group does not run. Tier 1 said labs need registration; the events page does not say that.

records.name: Women Matter Alliance
records.summary: A group that supports domestic violence survivors with legal advocacy, social and mental health help, and job coaching. It serves survivors of all genders, including LGBTQ+ survivors, and welcomes volunteers with skills such as legal advice and social media.
records.what_you_do: Survivors can ask about the group's legal advocacy, social and mental health services, and job coaching. Volunteers bring skills such as legal advice, social media, accounting, or help recruiting advisors and board members.

cost.text: The site does not say whether services cost anything.

first_step.how: Call 1.800.799.7233 or use the contact form on the website to ask about services, or about volunteering your skills.
first_step.basis: The site gives a phone line and a contact form, but says nothing about who qualifies for services, what a first contact involves, or how volunteers are placed, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: Homepage and FAQ give no intake steps, hours, eligibility, locations, or accessibility details, so no what_to_expect is recorded. The only dated item is a 2024 copyright footer, which is not evidence, so status stays probably_active. The FAQ gives the phone and email for questions it does not answer and does not say whether they handle service requests. Domestic violence wording on the homepage was confirmed on a second read; summary unchanged.

records.name: A Sister's Heart
records.summary: A family-led nonprofit that supports people with breast cancer, survivors, and their families with education, emotional support, and events such as an annual tea party for survivors.
records.what_you_do: Take part in the group's events, such as My Day, a self-care day with guided workshops and mindfulness activities for people in treatment, or the annual tea party for survivors. The site does not explain how to join the community or volunteer.

schedule.text: There is no regular meeting schedule. The group holds events from time to time, including an annual tea party for survivors.

cost.text: The site lists no membership fees. Its only money option is a donate button.

first_step.how: Email asistersheartinfo@gmail.com to ask about the next event, or how to join A Sisters Community, since the site does not explain joining.
first_step.basis: The most recent event listed asked people to RSVP by phone, and a luncheon was invite only. The site does not say how to join the group or when the next open event is.
first_step.what_to_expect: The My Day event is a self-care day with guided workshops and mindfulness activities for people in treatment. The site does not say how long it runs or who leads it, so ask by email before you go.
first_visit_tips: Ask by email for the date of the next event, since the events page lists only past events.
Plan to RSVP ahead, because the most recent community day asked for RSVPs by phone.

records.notes: Events page lists four past events, from February 2025 to May 2026. The newest is My Day Cafe on May 16, 2026, 10 am to 4 pm, free admission, with RSVPs by phone to three family members; those numbers are not recorded here. One 2025 tea event was in Maryland, not Philadelphia. The March 2025 luncheon was invite only. Founding date and history are not stated. The A Sisters Community page describes nothing beyond its name, so how the community works is unknown. Status moved from probably_active to active on the May 2026 event. Contact name corrected to Rae Royster, as the events and about pages spell it.

records.name: Back on Track Community Outreach Services
records.summary: A community outreach nonprofit with its office in Harrisburg. It says it serves Harrisburg, Philadelphia, and nearby tri-county areas, and it describes workshops, support groups, community events, and help finding resources.
records.what_you_do: Contact the group by its contact form or email to ask about workshops, support groups, and events, and what is running in Philadelphia. The site says people can reach out to get help, volunteer, or partner, but does not describe how volunteering works.

cost.text: The site does not state a cost for its programs.

first_step.how: Email backontrack.comserv@gmail.com or use the contact form to ask which workshops, support groups, or events are running in Philadelphia, and how to join one.
first_step.basis: The site names workshops and support groups but gives no sign-up steps, schedule, or Philadelphia meeting place, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: The website office is in Harrisburg (1821 Fulton Street). The IRS address on file is in Philadelphia and is kept. The site names Philadelphia as part of its service area but names no Philadelphia program, meeting place, or contact, so the reviewer should decide whether this stays a Philadelphia listing. Programs are described only in general terms, so no what_to_expect is recorded. Footers show 2025 to 2026 copyright, which is not evidence. Tier 1 drop_in false was removed because the site does not say whether drop in is possible. Contact name Terrence Lewis is carried from tier 1 and does not appear on the pages read.

records.name: Chloe's Way
records.summary: A community nonprofit that helps families and individuals in hardship with food boxes, clothing, and hygiene kits. In the summer it sponsors lunches for local kids and runs a youth enrichment program for 4th to 6th graders, and it offers scholarships to high school seniors.
records.what_you_do: Volunteers can help at food distributions and community events, pack and sort food boxes, clothing, and hygiene kits, deliver groceries to older neighbors, and help with summer meals (meal help, set-up, and clean-up). Donors can give through the donate page.

schedule.text: Summer lunch support and the youth summer enrichment program run during the summer, and the site gives no exact dates.

cost.text: Help is free; donations are welcome.

first_step.how: Email kera@chloesway.org or call (215) 316-4450 to ask how to volunteer for the summer lunch or the youth summer enrichment program.
first_step.basis: The get-involved page invites volunteers and gives a phone number and email to ask. The homepage join button is still a placeholder, so the first step is a message.
first_step.what_to_expect: Volunteer jobs include meal help, set-up, and clean-up at summer lunches, and packing and sorting food boxes, clothing, and hygiene kits. The site does not say how long a shift lasts, whether there is training, or who you would work with, so ask when you make contact.
first_visit_tips: Email before you come, since the site does not list volunteer shift times or places.
Ask whether the summer lunch shifts are in Philadelphia, since the site also names Richmond, Virginia.

records.notes: Summer lunch and youth enrichment are described on the homepage, not the programs page. Homepage volunteer and youth join buttons link to nothing, so email and phone are the working route. The news page has three undated posts and no program news. The 2026 mentions there are file names and a copyright footer, not evidence, so last_sign_of_life stays at March 2026, the scholarship deadline on the homepage (up to $2,500, due March 31, 2026). The site has an accessibility toolbar and a language menu listing about 40 languages, but does not confirm how complete the translations are, so no languages are recorded. Support email support@chloesway.org appears in the footer and is not recorded.

records.name: Creative Arts and Healing Enterprises
records.summary: An arts and healing workshop run by the artist Terrence Gore. The Art of Healing workshop mixes art-making with dance, music, and nutrition education, and it can be held for groups of any size in places such as hospitals, public spaces, or homes.
records.what_you_do: Take part in a workshop session. The Art of Healing mixes art-making with dance, music, and nutrition education, and the site also lists a Rehabilitation workshop. Use the contact form to ask about upcoming sessions.

schedule.text: The site lists no regular meeting times. Sessions can be run for groups of any size in other venues.

cost.text: The site does not state a fee for the workshops.

first_step.how: Use the contact form at terrencelgore.com/contact, or email aneye4it64@gmail.com, to ask which workshop sessions are coming up and whether an individual can join one.
first_step.basis: The site says the workshop can be run for groups in other venues, and it shows no dates, prices, or sign-up steps, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The Art of Healing combines interactive art-making with dance, music, and nutrition education, and it is run for groups. The site does not say how long a session lasts, how many people attend, or what it costs, so ask first.
first_visit_tips: Name the workshop you are interested in when you write, The Art of Healing or Rehabilitation.
Ask for the next session date and place, since the site lists no upcoming sessions.

records.notes: The site is thin. The home page shows only the title and menu, and the workshop pages give examples but no dates, prices, or sign-up steps. The only address on file is an IRS apartment address (4050 Haverford Ave Apt 101) that looks like a residence. It is not restated here and is still on the record from tier 1, so the reviewer should decide whether to keep it. The Philadelphia artist description from tier 1 is not on the site, so the summary no longer says it. Philadelphia venues appear only as past examples (Penn Museum, The Painted Bride). The Rehabilitation post is dated October 1, 2025, an older sign of life. The exhibitions page lists an April 18 event under a 2026 heading, which is the newest evidence. The workshop is described as aimed at people with disabilities but open to anyone, so no community tag is added.

records.name: Greenest
records.summary: Runs Greentool, an online tool for finding products, services, and companies that help or harm the environment. Volunteers research and edit its data through an online portal.
records.what_you_do: Volunteers apply for remote roles on greenest.org, such as Environmental Analyst or Citizen Scientist, to research and edit the data in the portal. Anyone can also submit a business or product for review through the review request form.

cost.text: The listed roles are unpaid volunteer positions. The site does not say whether there is any fee.

first_step.how: Open greenest.org/careers/all and apply for a remote analyst role, or send a business or product to the review request form.
first_step.basis: Portal editing requires a volunteer application, so the way in is an application step. The public review forms are open to anyone but ask for business details.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not say how much time a volunteer role takes, what training is given, or how long an application takes. The public review form asks for a business name, a website, and a description, and the site does not say how long a review takes.
first_visit_tips: If no role matches your skills, the careers page says you can send a resume through the Contact Us page.
The review request form is a way to help without applying for a role.

records.notes: All six listed roles are remote, unpaid volunteer positions: Environmental Analyst I, Citizen Scientist, UX Designer, Python/Flask Web Developer, Grant Writer, and one listing titled Test 2026 that looks like a test entry and is not described here. No time commitment, training, or deadlines are stated. IRS lists Philadelphia, but the work is fully online, so the reviewer may decide whether an online only group belongs in a Philadelphia directory. The IRS address on file is an apartment address (4104 Walnut St Apt 2R) that looks like a residence. It is not restated here and is still on the record from tier 1, so the reviewer should decide. Copyright footers (2025, 2026) are not evidence, so status stays probably_active. Added citizen_science because the Citizen Scientist role is listed.
